rationale: The static parallel-merge template reproduces Clarke-Wright with strong solution quality (baseline mean 24.23, close to the best dev_24 cw_parallel_merge raw mean 16.22 after scaling) and low postprocess need. It has full completion on both n=40 and n=200, with p95 solve times of 7.64 ms and 10.23 ms — respectively 30.6% and 40.9% of the 25 ms target, safely under the 55% headroom threshold. The sequential template has worse solution quality (higher gap, 12.56% postprocess drop, 10.68% remaining gap) despite more headroom, while the dynamic template fails the headroom and completion criteria (90% on n=40, 75% on n=200, p95 ≈ 25 ms = 100% of budget). Therefore static parallel-merge offers the best quality–timing tradeoff.
